title: Information-Theoretic Time
html:
Definition. Information-Theoretic Time

Definition. Let (\mathbf{C}, A, \tau) be a quantum observable universe with braiding-induced ordering \prec_c (ordering–jet compatibility). Let f_q(z) = z^2 + c(q) be the Julia set iteration on the exceptional divisor (Julia set of Reeb flow).

The information-theoretic time at substrate parameter q is the cumulative Reeb operation count:

  \mathcal{T}(q)  :=  \sum_{n=0}^{N-1} 1
  =  N

where N is the total number of iterations of f_q applied since a reference configuration \mathcal{S}_0 (bundle initial conditions). Each iteration advances the admissible ordering by one step. The count \mathcal{T} determines the position in the braiding-induced ordering \prec_c propagated through the jet tower.
